question: Can two finite machines with identical observed positive traces force refusal of object closure until a complete finite coverage certificate is supplied, while a later delayed witness falsifies the unsafe trace-only close?
level: Research-local exact finite prefix carrier extending one uncompleted Research 0090 control; no native Rust judgment, Keraia mass transfer, M6 filler or universality claim

program_domains: fresh reuse: all binary words of width 3
objects.machine: receiver-selected map from accepted program to first reveal stage
objects.observation: ordered positive events visible through an exact nonnegative integer stage
objects.negative_information: only a complete receiver-selected finite coverage certificate may classify an unobserved program as rejected

acceptance: At the early stage each pair has byte-identical positive traces
Any deterministic trace-only rule therefore returns the same proposal for both machines
The unsafe proposal is replayably falsified by the delayed positive event
The guarded receiver returns CertificateObstruction without complete coverage and never converts timeout into a negative certificate
A complete finite tell-tale certificate permits ObjectClosed and preserves positives, negatives, universe, stage and history
At the late stage the two histories and lower accepted counts diverge
Malformed, incomplete, context-changed and Boolean/float-substituted receipts are refused
A fresh process reproduces all deterministic evidence
exit: Finish the two fixed pairs and controls, or stop on mismatch, invalid certificate, resource exhaustion or implementation failure. No automatic widening or retry.
